stories.title: Every Cure: using AI to find new uses for drugs already on the shelf
points: A nonprofit co-founded by Dr David Fajgenbaum, in remission for over 11 years thanks to a repurposed drug.
Its AI analyses the world’s knowledge of drugs and diseases to rank the most promising repurposing ideas.
Anyone can suggest repurposing ideas, volunteer as an expert, or donate.
stories.why: The fastest new treatment may already be sitting in a pharmacy.
stories.other: Old, cheap drugs earn little for anyone. Who pays for the costly trials needed to prove each new use?

stories.title: Noel Tata seeks the video and minutes of the meeting that reappointed Chandrasekaran
points: In a September 30 letter, the Tata Trusts chairman asked the Tata Sons board for the recording and minutes of its September 17 meeting, executives said.
He says he wasn’t given enough time to present former CJI DY Chandrachud’s view that the chairman’s casting vote can’t override the trust nominees’ affirmative rights.
He also questions why the board obtained two more opinions after the vote, from former CJI UU Lalit and retired Justice BN Srikrishna; both upheld it.
stories.why: The fight over Tata’s top job has moved from boardroom to lawyers.
stories.other: Three legal opinions back the vote, and an independent lawyer says a director has no unfettered right to a board video. Is this governance, or a lost vote relitigated?

stories.title: India goes FTA shopping at the G20, with Piyush Goyal working the room
points: In Milwaukee, Goyal met ministers from 10 countries and the EU on deals at every stage, from talks to pacts already in force.
USTR Jamieson Greer says the India-US interim deal is in the “short strokes”, but an announcement isn’t imminent.
The India-EU FTA awaits signature, the India-Canada CEPA targets year-end, and the India-New Zealand FTA takes effect on October 20.
stories.why: Signing is the easy part; exporters still have to use these deals.
stories.other: More deals also mean more imports and tougher rivals at home. Do Indian firms gain more access than they give up?

stories.title: RBI governor warns against complacency amid external headwinds
points: Sanjay Malhotra called India’s financial system “very resilient”, but said long spells of stability encourage risk-taking and leverage.
He flagged high global debt, stretched AI valuations, leverage outside banks and private credit, with AI-driven cyber risk the most immediate.
The US 10-year Treasury touched a 24-year high of 5.34% on Thursday; India’s bond yields have risen more slowly than peers’.
stories.why: Calm periods are when banks take the risks that hurt later.
stories.other: He sees no imminent stress, and says an AI-valuation correction abroad could even send capital to India. Warning, or routine caution?

stories.title: China, America and the new Great Game
points: Rana Foroohar likens the US-China rivalry to the 19th-century Britain-Russia Great Game: decades of moves, not one war.
China owns 60% of Peru’s Chancay megaport, and almost half the leading container ports outside China have some Chinese ownership or operations.
Her verdict: outside nations such as India, Japan, Canada, the Gulf states and the EU may decide the outcome.
stories.why: India is a swing player in this contest, not a bystander.
stories.other: She concedes the US still has the reserve currency, the richest tech firms and free sea lanes; there may be no single winner.

stories.title: How the French bond trade backfired on investors
points: Hedge funds piled into leveraged bets on French debt over the summer, figuring French politics wouldn’t get much rockier.
A widening poll lead for Marine Le Pen and a poorly received budget plan sparked selling; short-term yields swung up to 0.40 points over two days.
France’s €3.5tn government bond market is Europe’s largest, and foreigners own more than half of it.
stories.why: Crowded trades exit through a narrow door.
stories.other: PGIM’s Robert Tipp says forced selling, not a change in France’s creditworthiness, drove the rout, and the ECB ultimately backstops eurozone bonds.

stories.title: Americans can’t stop watching people pay down their debt
points: On TikTok, users share the exact amount they owe and post updates as it goes up or down.
Flight attendant Rodney Morgan’s $40,058 debt video drew 1.5M views, against about 100,000 for his best earlier posts.
Views can pay bills: influencer Kayla Rose cleared more than $25,000 of card debt with video income.
stories.why: Money shame is turning into accountability, and income.
stories.other: When debt videos earn money, does the audience reward the habit as much as the payoff?

stories.title: Every Cure set to get up to $76M from ARPA-H to test its AI picks
points: A three-year phase from 2026 moves AI-picked ideas toward patients.
It builds on an earlier $48.3M ARPA-H contract that built the MATRIX platform.
stories.why: US public money is betting on AI-found cures.
stories.other: AI predictions still have to survive trials; most drug candidates don’t.

stories.title: Polymarket’s Alpha traders: the secret chat turning wars and elections into profit
points: About 30 members, mostly Gen Z, pool research in an invitation-only Discord; they’ve made an estimated $40mn on Polymarket since 2024.
A CEPR study found two-thirds of Polymarket users lost money; 0.1% of profitable traders captured half the profits.
Polymarket and Kalshi averaged about $1.6bn a day in August, up nearly 2,000% in a year.
stories.why: A few sharps win; most bettors are the liquidity they feed on.
stories.other: Members call it skill, not luck. One, a PhD student now attending gambling-addiction meetings, says the real harm is the story that this is democratised finance.
